source_construct: on start, compare the native version with the bundled package.json version; when they differ, remember it in sessionStorage and reload the page with `?prism-version=` so WebView2 drops a cached old bundle
target_translation: Not ported. It exists only because WebView2 can serve a cached entry document after the native binary updates. The GPUI binary is the UI, so there is no separate bundle to go stale.

source_construct: on `prism-toggle` with open=false: hide("native"). With open=true: dismiss transient UI, reset the palette (no leftover query, selection, or settings), close settings, clear the close timer, reduce phase with "open"; when the result is Visible, present the window: not presented -> "present-failed"; presented -> focus the search input; a rejected present -> "present-failed"
target_translation: Root view handles `CoreEvent::Toggle(PalettePresentation { open, .. })` in the same order: close -> `hide(Native)`; open -> `TransientUi::dismiss_all`, `palette.reset()`, `app.set_open_settings(false)`, drop `close_task`, `phase = reduce(phase, Open)`; when Visible, spawn `backend.present_palette()`: Ok(false) or Err -> reduce PresentFailed; Ok(true) -> focus_search.

source_construct: on mount, ask isWindowVisible(); if the native window is already visible while React thinks it is hidden, enter "preparing" (or "visible" outside Tauri)
target_translation: Not ported. It repairs a race where the web page loads after the native window was shown (comment :181-183). In GPUI the root view is created together with its window, and the window's visibility is owned by prism-app, so the two states cannot diverge.

source_construct: `useEffect(() => () => clearCloseTimer())`
target_translation: Dropping the root view drops `close_task`.

source_construct: while phase is "preparing": present the native window after the DOM is committed; on success wait one animation frame, then reduce "presented" and focus the search input; on failure reduce "present-failed"; a phase change cancels the pending steps
target_translation: When phase becomes Preparing, the root view renders the prepared frame, then spawns `backend.present_palette()` in `present_task` (replaced on each phase change, which cancels). Ok(true) -> `window.on_next_frame(|…| { phase = reduce(phase, Presented); focus_search })`; Ok(false) or Err -> reduce PresentFailed.

source_construct: focus items by index with wrap; open cancels a pending close timer, clears closing, opens, and focuses the item on the next animation frame; close(animate) snaps or animates for POPOVER_MOTION_MS, ignoring a close when already closed
target_translation: View fields `open`, `closing`, `close_task: Option<Task<()>>`, item FocusHandles. `open_menu(index)` drops `close_task`, sets open, focuses item `index mod len` on the next frame. `close_menu(animate)` returns when neither open nor closing; drops `close_task`; snap -> closed now; animate -> closing, then a POPOVER_MOTION_MS task closes it.

symbol: outside press, palette close, settings open
source_construct: while open: a pointer press outside the menu root closes it with animation; prism:close and transient dismiss close it at once; opening settings closes it at once; unmount clears the close timer
target_translation: While open: `on_mouse_down_out` on the menu root -> close_menu(true); registered with TransientUi and the root's close broadcast -> close_menu(false); observe AppState.open_settings -> close_menu(false) when it becomes true. Dropping the view drops `close_task`.

source_construct: ignore while busy; perform the power action; on success close the menu and broadcast prism:close; on error toast "Could not {shut down|lock|sleep|restart…}" with the error text; clear busy
target_translation: `busy: Option<PowerAction>`; task runs `backend.perform_power_action(action)`; Ok -> open=false and `RootView::close_palette`; Err -> toast title `Could not shut down` for shutdown, else `Could not {action}`.

source_construct: ArrowDown/ArrowUp move with wrap from the focused item (focusItem uses modulo), Home/End, Escape closes with animation and returns focus to the trigger button
target_translation: Menu key context with the same keys; Escape -> close_menu(true) then focus the trigger's FocusHandle.

source_construct: ignore when the combo is current or busy; register with the OS first (`setShortcut`), then persist; toasts "Shortcut set" (detail: displayShortcut(combo)) or "Shortcut not changed" (detail: error)
target_translation: `busy: bool`; task runs `backend.set_shortcut(combo)` first and only on Ok calls `app.update_settings(shortcut)` (persistence follows success, as the comment at :71-72 requires). Same toast titles and details.

source_construct: ignore when unchanged or busy; apply in the OS, then persist; error toast "Taskbar not changed"
target_translation: Same shape as applyShortcut: `backend.set_taskbar_alignment(a)` then `update_settings`; Err -> toast "Taskbar not changed" with the error text.

source_construct: while a group's picker is open: focus its search field; a pointer press outside the picker closes it
target_translation: Opening sets `open_group_id` and focuses the search input's FocusHandle; `on_mouse_down_out` on the picker root sets `open_group_id = None`.

source_construct: while open: request icons for the first 512 filtered apps that have no icon and were not requested; merge results; on failure forget the request so it can retry
target_translation: View fields `picker_icons: HashMap<String, String>`, `requested: HashSet<String>`; when the filter or the open group changes, compute the same missing set (cap 512), mark requested, spawn `backend.get_app_icons(ids)`; Ok -> merge; Err -> remove the ids from `requested`.

source_construct: clears the filter text and focuses the filter input
target_translation: on_click: set the query to "" and focus the filter input's FocusHandle.

source_construct: reads the app version once on mount
target_translation: `env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION")` of prism-app (the same version as the release; check-version keeps them equal). No async call.

source_construct: X and backdrop: animate out for 150 ms, then close; ignored while closing. A fresh open cancels a pending close and clears `closing`; closing settings also clears the reset confirmation
target_translation: `closing: bool`, `close_task: Option<Task<()>>`. request_close: if closing return; closing = true; task sleeps 150 ms then `app.set_open_settings(false)`. Observe AppState.open_settings: on true drop close_task and set closing = false; on false set reset_confirming = false. Dropping the view drops the task.

source_construct: two-step reset (first click arms, second click resets) with busy guard and toasts "Settings reset" / "Settings not reset"; retrySave with busy guard and error toast "Settings still not saved" (kind error)
target_translation: `reset_confirming`, `reset_busy`, `retry_save_busy` fields; tasks call `app.reset_settings()` and `app.retry_persistence()`; same titles, details ("Prism is back to its defaults"), and the error kind for the retry toast.

symbol: focus on open and restore on close
source_construct: on open focus the first `[data-autofocus]`, button, or switch in the panel; on close focus the palette's settings trigger (`[data-settings-trigger]`)
target_translation: The sheet holds FocusHandles for its controls in order and an optional autofocus handle; on open focus the autofocus handle or the first control; on close the root view focuses the settings trigger's FocusHandle (owned by the palette header).

source_construct: ignored while composing; Escape closes at once (no animation); Tab and Shift+Tab wrap focus between the first and last enabled, visible, tabbable controls
target_translation: Key context on the panel: Escape -> `set_open_settings(false)` (snap, unlike request_close); Tab / Shift+Tab -> GPUI tab order restricted to the panel's focus handles, wrapping at both ends (disabled and hidden controls are not in the list).

source_construct: load prism.json once; sanitize settings and history (judge settings.*, history.*); settings changed while a load error was active are merged over the loaded values; history changed during the error is kept; a load error sets the message "Could not load settings: {error}. Repair prism.json, then retry. Saving is paused to preserve your file." and pauses saving; `ready` turns true when the read finishes either way; the result is ignored after unmount
target_translation: AppState fields `ready`, `state_load_error: Option<String>`, `settings_changed_after_load_error: SettingsPatch`, `history_changed_after_load_error: bool`, `state_read: Shared<Task<()>>` (flush awaits it). The load task applies the same merge order and the same message text. Dropping AppState drops the task.

source_construct: after ready: read the system theme once, then follow theme-change events
target_translation: After ready, `backend.get_system_theme()` once, plus the `CoreEvent::ThemeChanged` subscription (bridge listen row). Both set `system_theme`.

source_construct: if loading had failed: reload, re-sanitize, re-apply the changes made during the error, clear the error; a second load failure sets the same message and rethrows; then flush
target_translation: Same steps as a method returning `Task<Result<(), String>>`; the error text is identical to the initial-load message.

source_construct: clear the persist timer and every toast timer
target_translation: Dropping AppState drops `persist_timer` and `toast_tasks`. No explicit code.

source_construct: wait for the initial read; refuse while a load error is active; native first: set the default shortcut, then the default taskbar alignment; if alignment fails, roll back alignment and shortcut and throw the composed message (three message shapes: shortcut rollback failed, alignment rollback failed, plain error); on success replace settings with defaults (empty pins and groups, default quick access and section order) and schedule a save
target_translation: Method `reset_settings(cx) -> Task<Result<(), String>>` with the same order and the same three error strings ("Reset stopped: {e}. Shortcut restoration also failed: {r}. The shortcut remains Win.{ Taskbar restoration failed: {a}.}" ; "Reset stopped: {e}. Could not restore taskbar alignment: {a}. Select the alignment again to retry."; or the original error). When the shortcut rollback fails, settings.shortcut becomes the default.

source_construct: flush persistence, then quit; on error the toast "Could not quit Prism" with detail "Your changes are still open. {error}" (kind error)
target_translation: `quit(cx)`: await flush, then `backend.quit_app()`; Err -> the same toast.

source_construct: whenever `persistenceError` becomes non-empty: toast "Settings need attention" / "Open Settings to review the error and retry saving." (kind error)
target_translation: The setter of `persistence_error` shows the toast when the new value is Some. Same text.

source_construct: with the accent/theme effect: `setOsdAccent(settings.accent)`, errors ignored
target_translation: On accent change after ready: `backend.set_osd_accent(accent)`, result ignored. (The accent/theme row covers the Theme global.)

source_construct: after ready and on each effective-theme change: `setWindowStyle(theme)`; error toast "Appearance not applied" (kind error)
target_translation: `backend.set_window_style(theme)` for the GPUI window's HWND (prism-core keeps the native style code); Err -> same toast.

source_construct: on width change after ready: with no previous width, the same width, or reduced motion, set the width at once; otherwise animate from the rendered width to the target over 240 ms with ease-out cubic `1 - (1 - t)^3`, rounding to whole pixels, sending a native resize at most every 45 ms and always at the end; an error at the end shows "Window width not applied" / "Try selecting the width again. {error}" (kind error); a new width cancels the running animation
target_translation: `width_task: Option<Task<()>>` replaced on each change; the task steps on each frame (`window.request_animation_frame` / timer at frame rate), computes the same eased value, throttles `backend.set_window_width(px)` to 45 ms, and sends the final value. Reduced motion (the reduced-motion row) skips to the target. Same toast.

source_construct: after ready and on change: set the window's always-on-top; error toast "Always on top not applied" / "Toggle the setting to retry. {error}"
target_translation: prism-app sets the window level (GPUI `WindowKind::PopUp`/topmost, or `SetWindowPos(HWND_TOPMOST/NOTOPMOST)` through prism-core on the GPUI HWND). Same toast.
status: needs-spike: which GPUI 0.2.2 window option toggles topmost at runtime on Windows; fallback is SetWindowPos on the raw HWND

source_construct: after ready and on change: `setViewZoom(percent)`, which in Tauri sets the WebView zoom factor (percent / 100); error toast "Zoom not applied" / "Choose a zoom level to retry. {error}"
target_translation: All UI sizes are expressed in rems (rule:classname and theme.rs), and the root sets `window.set_rem_size(BASE_REM * percent / 100)` so the whole UI scales like the WebView zoom. The window size itself does not change (WebView zoom does not resize the window). Same toast text on failure.

source_construct: after ready and on change: `setTaskbarScrollVolume(settings.taskbarScrollVolume ?? true)`; error toast "Taskbar volume control not applied" / "Toggle the setting to retry. {error}"
target_translation: `backend.set_taskbar_scroll_volume(value)` with the same default true; same toast.

source_construct: after ready: on `win-mode-failed` show "Win-key mode disabled" with the reason (kind error) and set the shortcut back to the default
target_translation: Subscription to `CoreEvent::WinModeFailed(reason)`: same toast, then `update_settings(shortcut = DEFAULT)`.

symbol: initial apps and Quick Access load
source_construct: load the app list (error flag on failure, `appsLoaded` true either way) and the Quick Access list (errors ignored); results ignored after unmount
target_translation: PaletteState fields `apps`, `apps_error`, `apps_loaded`, `quick_access`; two tasks started at creation calling `backend.get_apps()` and `backend.get_quick_access()`. Dropping the entity drops them.

source_construct: on `apps-updated`: reload the app list; on success set apps, clear the error, mark loaded, bump `appsRevision` (which re-runs Phase 1 for the open query); on failure set the error flag
target_translation: Subscription to `CoreEvent::AppsUpdated`: same steps; `apps_revision += 1` triggers the Phase 1 refresh method.

source_construct: collect file paths from history ids; with none, clear the existing set at once; else ask `existing_paths` and apply the answer only if it is still the latest request (old rows stay visible meanwhile); errors ignored. Runs when history changes and when the window gains focus
target_translation: `history_path_request: u64`, `existing_history_paths: HashSet<String>`; method `validate_history_paths(cx)` with the same guard; called from the history setter and from the window-activation observer (activated only).

source_construct: for existing image files in history (png, jpg, jpeg, gif, bmp, webp by extension), request thumbnails not cached or in flight; apply only if the thumbnail epoch is unchanged; remember results (including null) in the cache; on error clear in-flight; bump the thumbnail revision
target_translation: PaletteState `thumbnail_cache: HashMap<String, Option<String>>`, `thumbnail_in_flight: HashSet<String>`, `thumbnail_epoch: u64`, `thumbnail_revision: u64`; same extension list and epoch guard; task calls `backend.get_file_thumbnails(paths)`.

source_construct: on `file-index-updated`: bump the thumbnail epoch, clear the cache and in-flight set, strip thumbnails from current file results, bump the thumbnail revision and the file index tick (re-runs the file search), mark the file status unknown, re-validate history paths
target_translation: Subscription to `CoreEvent::FileIndexUpdated` doing the same steps in the same order.

source_construct: on query, history, or apps revision change: empty trimmed query -> phase1 = None; else query Phase 1 with the trimmed text and the 20 newest history entries ({id, title}); apply only if still the latest request; an empty `response.query` or an error -> None
target_translation: `phase1_request: u64`, `phase1_task: Option<Task<()>>` replaced on each change; `backend.query_phase1(text, recent)`; same guard and the same None cases.

source_construct: refreshPowerPlans(text): new request id; empty -> []; else query and apply if latest (rethrows errors after clearing). The query effect clears the list at once, then after POWER_PLAN_QUERY_DELAY_MS (50 ms) queries if the text is non-empty, applying only the latest answer; errors -> []
target_translation: `power_plan_request: u64`, `power_plan_task: Option<Task<()>>`; on query change: clear `power_plans`, bump the id, start a task that sleeps 50 ms then calls `backend.query_power_plans(text)`. `refresh_power_plans(text) -> Task<Result<Vec<PowerPlanHit>, String>>` for runItem.

source_construct: force a rescan; on success cancel any icon retry, clear the settled and attempt sets, drop all icons, set apps, clear the error, bump the icon retry tick; on failure set the error flag; loaded true at the end
target_translation: Method calling `backend.refresh_apps()` with the same resets, including dropping `icon_retry`.

source_construct: clear the icon retry timer
target_translation: Dropping PaletteState drops `icon_retry`.

source_construct: move(delta) clamps to [0, len-1] (0 when empty) and clears the pending target; select(i) sets it; when the list shrinks, clamp the selection; when a selection target id is pending and appears in the new list, select it once
target_translation: `selected: usize`, `selection_target: Option<String>`; the same methods; clamping and retargeting run in the method that rebuilds `flat_items` (no effect needed).

source_construct: power plan rows: run; if the query changed meanwhile, toast "Power plan changed" (detail: title) and stop; else refresh plans for the submitted query, re-select the same row if the query is still the same, toast "Power plan changed"; a refresh error -> toast "Power plan changed" / "Could not refresh the list: {error}". Clipboard rows: run only. Window rows and all others: run, THEN hide_palette (sequential, never parallel: foreground rights). Then push history (id, historyTitle); for `action::` rows call accept_intent(query (untrimmed), id without "action::"), not awaited; for clipboard rows toast "Copied to clipboard" (detail: toastDetail or title). Any error: power plan -> "Power plan not changed" / error; else "Couldn’t open item" / title
target_translation: `PaletteState::run_item(item, cx) -> Task<()>` with exactly this order: `execute(item.actions.run)`; `backend.hide_palette(false)` after it for non-clipboard, non-power-plan rows; `app.push_history`; `backend.accept_intent(query_untrimmed, action_id)` fire-and-forget; toasts with the same texts (note the typographic apostrophe in "Couldn’t open item"). The judge cannot observe this sequence (golden-scenarios records closures only); the Step 6 UI scenario list must cover it.

source_construct: runSelected runs the selected row if any. runItemAsAdmin: no-op without runAsAdmin; run it, then hide (same ordering as runItem), push history; error toast "Could not run as administrator" / error
target_translation: Methods with the same order; elevation then `hide_palette(false)` then history.

source_construct: rebuild: mark indexing and call rebuild (errors ignored); retry: bump the file index tick; reset: empty query, selection 0
target_translation: Methods: `backend.rebuild_file_index()` after `file_indexing = true`; `file_index_tick += 1` (re-runs the file search); `set_query("")` and `selected = 0`.

source_construct: close the row menu, then focus the search input on the next frame when restoring focus; open: skip rows with no actions, select the row, menu height = actions × 36 + 8, clamp the position; pin toggle on app rows: unpin -> toast "Unpinned"; at PINNED_APP_LIMIT -> toast "Pin limit reached" / "Unpin an app before adding {title}"; pin -> toast "Pinned"; refocus the input on the next frame after a change
target_translation: Palette view methods with the same rules; "next frame" focus uses `window.on_next_frame`. Menu height constant 36 per action plus 8, passed to `clamp_context_menu_position`.

source_construct: pointer moves coalesced to one apply per animation frame; finish applies the pending move, then, when active with a target, reorders `sectionOrder` (reorderSections) or `appGroups` (reorderAppGroups) and persists; cancel drops pending work
target_translation: `CategoryDrag` state on the view; mouse-move handler stores the latest point and schedules one `on_next_frame` apply when none is pending; finish/cancel the same. Reordering uses the ported `types::reorder_sections` / `reorder_app_groups` (judge types.reorder*).
status: needs-spike: GPUI drag of a header with a floating preview (see the reorder-drag row)

source_construct: moves coalesced per frame; finish applies the pending move, reorders when active with a target item, and returns whether the drag was active (callers use it to suppress the click); an active drag that ends or is cancelled animates the preview out for 110 ms
target_translation: `ReorderDrag` state, `preview_leaving` with a 110 ms `Task`, the same frame coalescing; `finish` returns the active flag so the row's click handler can ignore the release.

source_construct: after the pointer passes the drag threshold, release pointer capture and start a native OLE drag (`item.dragFile` -> start_file_drag), ignoring errors, then clear the drag state; moves coalesced per frame; finish returns whether the drag became active
target_translation: On threshold: end the GPUI drag and call `backend.start_file_drag(paths)` (prism-core drag.rs, OLE `DoDragDrop`) from the window's thread; errors ignored; state cleared afterwards.
status: needs-spike: OLE DoDragDrop must run on the STA thread that owns the GPUI window and must not deadlock GPUI's event loop; verify on this machine

source_construct: while any drag is active, Escape clears all three drag states; unmount cancels pending frames and the preview timer
target_translation: While a drag is active, the view's key context handles Escape by clearing the drag states (before list navigation sees it). Dropping the view drops pending frame callbacks and the 110 ms task.

source_construct: open the row menu for the selected row at (row right − 12, row top + 12), or the window center when the row is not rendered
target_translation: Each row records its painted bounds (stored by element id during prepaint); the keyboard path reads the selected row's bounds, else the window center.

source_construct: open settings -> close settings; else non-empty query -> clear it; else broadcast prism:close
target_translation: Same three-step order; the last step calls `RootView::close_palette` (prism:close row).

source_construct: after the selection changes, scroll the selected row into view with `block: "nearest"` (no scroll when it is already visible)
target_translation: The result list is a variable-height `list()` with a `ListState`; on selection change call its reveal method so the row becomes visible with the least scrolling.
status: needs-spike: confirm the GPUI 0.2.2 ListState method that scrolls minimally (reveal) rather than to the top

source_construct: open location / run as admin close the menu then run; toggle pin closes the menu, runs, toasts "Unpinned from taskbar" or "Pinned to taskbar" (detail: title); an error containing "prism-manual-pin-required" while pinning toasts "Windows blocks automatic pinning" / "Open {title}, then right-click its taskbar icon and choose \"Pin to taskbar\"."; other errors "Could not update taskbar pin"; properties errors "Could not open properties"
target_translation: Handlers for `ContextMenuEvent` with the same order and texts. The manual-pin check matches the same marker string returned by prism-core.

source_construct: reorder preview 232×54 at (x − 232 − 14, y − 27), clamped to 8 px inside the window; the category preview uses the same rule with its own size
target_translation: A deferred, absolutely positioned element with the same arithmetic using the window's content size. The constants (232, 54, 14, 8) are CSS px, which WebView zoom scales: multiply them by zoom / 100 so the preview keeps its look at every zoom level.

source_construct: callback props for retry and rebuild; the loading text appears only after loading has lasted 200 ms
target_translation: `announce_task: Option<Task<()>>` started when loading begins (200 ms, then show), dropped when loading ends. Callback props as in rule:closure-field@ui.tsx.

source_construct: stateless components receiving many callbacks (select, run, open menu, pin, remove history, move, the reorder and file drag callbacks)
target_translation: ResultRow becomes `RenderOnce` with a reference to the Palette view entity instead of 16 closures; its handlers call the view's methods directly (`palette_view.update(cx, |v, cx| v.run(item, cx))`). FileSearchErrorNotice takes two boxed callbacks.
